negativeTransitions: commit after stage but before admitted
two logical children staging the same physical ActorId
two native candidate generations staging the same scheduler slot
registering a still-staged physical replacement as a separate child
reusing a physically spawned candidate ActorId after cleanup-backed abort
reusing the same native scheduler slot and generation after abandoned RESTART

assumptions: The host-provided readiness and cleanup callbacks are truthful.
Publication and routing exclusion must be established separately by ActorRuntime/native scheduler.
A registry-only trace does not prove real actor spawning or cleanup.

implementationNotes.java: One pending ActorId is reserved by exactly one child; ActorGroup teardown fences commit.
implementationNotes.native: One physical scheduler slot may be staged by at most one child; panic routing and registry commit publish atomically.
implementationNotes.identityABA: Physical identity/generation is permanently retired when staging begins, even if admission fails or RESTART is cleaned and aborted.
implementationNotes.controlClose: A live native bridge must reject a READY replacement if its supervisor CONTROL process has closed.
implementationNotes.readinessRace: Current host readiness checks are observational; an atomic scheduler/CONTROL publication lease remains a release gate.
